minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to take all of Marshall Park phases 1, 2A and 2B to Town Meeting, plus OPM costs, as a debt exclusion.
minutes.summary: The commission met in person and spent most of the evening on the 60% design and cost estimates for Marshall Park, with the landscape architect present. It chose to bring phases one, two A and two B to Town Meeting, conditional on added owner's project manager costs. It also conditionally approved school use of the 90-foot diamond outfield, approved a revolving fund budget and an invoice, and approved two sets of minutes.

budget_items.what_was_said: The finance director asked for a vote on the budget amount for the revolving fund, which sets the ins and outs in the accounting system. It can still be amended by a committee vote.

Two cost estimators reconciled their 60% design estimates, narrowing the gap between them. The estimate is broken out by phase and includes general conditions, design contingency, overhead and profit, bonds and escalation.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park total for the vote
budget_items.what_was_said: The two estimating firms came in close together; the chair suggested using the higher number, plus OPM costs still to be confirmed.
A bathroom is estimated at a quarter million. Board of Health septic repair money cannot currently be used to connect to sewer.
The Select Board indicated the project would be a debt exclusion needing a Town Meeting vote and a ballot vote. Members discussed explaining the tax impact to voters.
An invoice for January design development costs was reviewed by the OPM, which recommended approval.
The commission is collecting comparable-community data on user fees and will likely hold a workshop in March or April; no fee changes are planned for the coming year.
The design adds roughly 130 spaces; a grant requires staying above a minimum space count.

decisions.decision: The commission agreed in principle to let the school use the outfield of the 90-foot diamond, so long as the dimensions work; the chair will have the contact connect with the facilities director.
Consensus to put the full Marshall Park project (phases 1, 2A, 2B) before Town Meeting, with the option to amend the article down to phase one if support is lacking.
The higher cost estimate will be used, conditional on the chair confirming extra owner's project manager costs with the OPM the next day.
No fee changes this year; a user fee workshop will be set for March or April if data comes in, possibly folded into a light April agenda.
The next regular meeting is aimed at March 19, and the chair will ask the clerk's office for the room.
Plan for two public information sessions on Marshall Park in April; the chair will email details.
Beach staffing will be put on the March agenda because of low lifeguard interest.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to take Marshall Park phases 1, 2A and 2B to Town Meeting, with added owner's project manager costs still to be confirmed.
The commission agreed to use the higher of two reconciled cost estimates for the vote, conditional on the chair confirming extra project manager costs the next day.
The Select Board indicated the project would be a debt exclusion, which needs both a Town Meeting vote and a ballot vote.
The commission reached consensus to put the full project forward, with the option to amend the article down to phase one if support is lacking.
Members conditionally approved school use of the 90-foot diamond outfield, approved a revolving fund budget and approved a January design invoice; vote counts were not audible.

why_it_matters: A debt exclusion raises property taxes above the levy cap for the life of the debt, so residents would be asked to vote at Town Meeting and again at the ballot on Marshall Park.
The final amount is not fixed: the estimate is still at the 60% design stage and owner's project manager costs are still to be added, so the figure voters see may differ from the one discussed.
watch_next: Two public information sessions on Marshall Park planned for April; the chair will email details.
Next regular meeting aimed at March 19, with a user fee workshop possible in March or April and beach staffing on the March agenda.
